title: Open an item in Explorer
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

open.issue: C1 (derived): from a FILE in the results, the person can jump to it in Explorer: missing
C2 (derived): from a FOLDER in the results, the person can jump to it in Explorer: missing
C3 (derived): 'act on it there' — the jump lands with the item selected or opened in an Explorer window: missing
C4 (derived): 'any file or folder in the results' — every results surface offers it (largest files list, folder tree, results list, and the unreadable-folders list where it names a folder): missing

odd-names-selected-exactly-in-explorer: needs first: A reveal path that does not depend on SHParseDisplayName(full path) for names ending in '.' or ' ', reserved device names such as 'con', and anything inside a folder with such a name. Un…

Does PS-007's 'jump to it in Explorer and act on it there' accept landing on the nearest addressable ancestor (with the item's name in the status line) for items whose names Explorer mis-parses: trailing '.' or ' ', reserved device names, and anything under such a folder? Or must those items be selected exactly? Exact selection needs the untested route the odd-names spike named (a child PIDL built through IShellFolder on the parent), which adds a component and changes Plan's contract.
PathOf as a switch over four row types versus a shared IHasPath interface (or one common property name) on the rows. The switch was kept because it is four types and needs no new abstraction.

Fallback landing: highlight the nearest addressable ancestor in its own parent (measured call shape, one mechanism) versus open the ancestor's contents through ShellExecute (lands where the person wants, second mechanism, unmeasured for long paths).

Gestures: context menu plus Ctrl+Enter only, with no double-click on the flat lists (largest files, top-level). Uniformity with the tree, where double-click expands, won over double-click on the lists.
Failure and fallback reporting through a single status line, rather than a dialog or a toast. Only the latest message is kept.
The two architecture rules cover the shell-API boundary and the UI-thread block. Someone may want a rule for the planner's purity, and the design judged that a testability concern, not a defect.

Ctrl+Enter on a results-list row during a live scan: each refresh replaces the list's items, so the focused ListBoxItem goes away and Ctrl+Enter then finds no row. The entry is disabled, so it never acts on a wrong target, but it does nothing. Validation recorded this as not reached. It needs a design decision, such as keeping focus or selection across refreshes, which is SL-039 territory.

docs/design/SL-039-live-results.md:74 ('560 by 620 and up') and docs/design/SL-044-folder-tree.md:60 ('its minimum stays 620') describe the minimum height before SL-047 raised it to 644. They are those slices' own design records, so I left them unedited. A note, or an SL-047 design doc recording the change, would close the drift code-review raised.
The O-029 status wording is not asserted by any test. A Core-side formatter test would pin it, but FormatRevealStatus lives in the App, which has no unit-test project.

not reached: Revealing a \\server\share root, or any item on a reachable SMB share. There is no share I may use: the loopback rig creates SMB client mappings, and the person's mapped Z: was left alone. Only Plan's unit tests cover the UNC root.
not reached: C:\ from the window's own tree root row. That needs a full scan of C:. C:\ was revealed through Core's RevealAsync, the call the window makes.

not reached: A physical mouse right-click and a physical Ctrl+Enter. Menus were opened as ContextMenuService opens them, and the key was delivered in-process (thread keyboard state plus a routed KeyDown), not through SendInput.

not reached: Ctrl+Enter on a results-list row during a live scan works only until the next refresh (≤250 ms). After that, focus is on the ListBox and the press does nothing. Measured, not a wrong target. It needs the design decision build-slice recorded.

not reached: Explorer at Windows' default hidden settings (Hidden=2, ShowSuperHidden=0). This machine is at Hidden=1, and registry settings are off-limits. Only the hidden note is checked, not whether hidden or system items get selected.

not reached: A literal E_ACCESSDENIED (0x80070005) from SHParseDisplayName or SHOpenFolderAndSelectItems. The real denial produced E_ABORT (0x80004004), and the real network failure was 0x80070043, not 0x80070035.
not reached: A real removable or network volume disappearing mid-session. This was simulated with a never-present drive letter, giving 0x8007000F rather than the 0x80070003 the unit test fakes.
not reached: A machine with LongPathsEnabled=0. The 633-character reveal was measured only here, with LongPathsEnabled=1 and 8.3 names on C:.
not reached: A folder, rather than a file, at depth 2 or more revealed from the tree. GetPath was checked at depth on files, and folder selection on folders at depth 1.
not reached: Display scaling other than 100% for the one-line status budget (24 px) and the 644 px minimum height.
